excerpt:
Bonds of the City of Brookland in the maximum aggregate principal amount of
$4,640,000 for the purpose of financing all or a portion of the costs of refunding
the City's Sales and Use Tax Refunding and Improvement Bonds, Series 2021 and,
in order to pay the bonds, the pledge of the existing 2% local sales and use tax
levied within the City by Ordinance No. 2015-25, adopted August 31, 2015, as
amended (the "2015 Tax"). The 2015 Tax expires on the first date on which the
2015 Tax can be administratively removed when (a) there are sufficient funds to
pay in full any outstanding bonds secured by a pledge of collections of the 2015
Tax and (b) the City Council determines that the purposes of the 2015 Tax cannot
be or cannot continue to be fulfilled because no bonds secured by a pledge of
collections of the 2015 Tax will be issued in the future.

excerpt:
Bonds of the City of Brookland in one or more series from time to time in the
maximum aggregate principal amount of $7,450,000 (the "2027 Park Improvement
Bonds") for the purpose of financing a portion of the costs of park and recreational
facilities and improvements, including particularly, without limitation, ball fields,
any land acquisition therefor, and any furnishings, equipment, utility adjustments
and lighting, street, parking, landscaping, signage and drainage improvements
related thereto or in support thereof and, in order to pay the bonds, the pledge of
the existing 2% local sales and use tax levied within the City by Ordinance No
2015-25, adopted August 31, 2015, as amended (the "2015 Tax"). The 2015 Tax
expires on the first date on which the 2015 Tax can be administratively removed
when (a) there are sufficient funds to pay in full any outstanding bonds secured by
a pledge of collections of the 2015 Tax and (b) the City Council determines that the
purposes of the 2015 Tax cannot be or cannot continue to be fulfilled because no
bonds secured by a pledge of collections of the 2015 Tax will be issued in the future.
A portion of the park and recreational facilities and improvements were financed
with proceeds of the City’s Sales and Use Tax Refunding and Improvement Bonds,
Series 2021, and the 2027 Park Improvement Bonds are proposed to finance the
remainder of the costs necessary to complete such facilities and improvements.

excerpt:
Bonds of the City of Brookland in one or more series from time to time in the
maximum aggregate principal amount of $3,445,000 (the "2027 Municipal
Building Improvement Bonds") for the purpose of financing a portion of the costs
of the acquisition and construction of a municipal building that will contain city
offices and a police station, any land acquisition therefor, and any furnishings,
equipment, utility adjustments and lighting, street, parking, landscaping, signage
and drainage improvements related thereto or in support thereof and, in order to
pay the bonds, the pledge of the existing 2% local sales and use tax levied within
the City by Ordinance No. 2015-25, adopted August 31, 2015, as amended (the
"2015 Tax"). The 2015 Tax expires on the first date on which the 2015 Tax can be
administratively removed when (a) there are sufficient funds to pay in full any
outstanding bonds secured by a pledge of collections of the 2015 Tax and (b) the
City Council determines that the purposes of the 2015 Tax cannot be or cannot
continue to be fulfilled because no bonds secured by a pledge of collections of the
2015 Tax will be issued in the future. A portion of the costs of acquiring and
constructing the municipal building was also financed with proceeds of the City’s
Sales and Use Tax Refunding and Improvement Bonds, Series 2021, and the 2027
Municipal Building Improvement Bonds are proposed to finance the remainder of
the costs necessary to complete such facilities.

excerpt:
Bonds of the City of Brookland in one or more series from time to time in the
maximum aggregate principal amount of $7,910,000 for the purpose of financing
all or a portion of the costs of constructing and improving streets and roads,
including particularly, without limitation, any paving, repair, curbing, gutter,
sidewalks, signage and drainage improvements, equipment and land acquisition
and street lighting, utility improvements and adjustments and traffic signals related
thereto or in support thereof and, in order to pay the bonds, the pledge of the existing
2% local sales and use tax levied within the City by Ordinance No 2015-25, adopted
August 31, 2015, as amended (the "2015 Tax"). The 2015 Tax expires on the first
date on which the 2015 Tax can be administratively removed when (a) there are
sufficient funds to pay in full any outstanding bonds secured by a pledge of
collections of the 2015 Tax and (b) the City Council determines that the purposes
of the 2015 Tax cannot be or cannot continue to be fulfilled because no bonds
secured by a pledge of collections of the 2015 Tax will be issued in the future. If
the bonds are approved, the City may, prior to the issuance of the bonds, obtain
such interim financing as permitted by Arkansas laws.
